properties.title: "What the Field Needs — Technology, Capacity, and People in the Age of Digital Public Goods"
properties.description:
Speakers from various United Nations entities share how technology actually works in the field — and what is still missing — in the closing keynote of FOSS4G 2026 Hiroshima.

The United Nations system is accelerating the adoption of open technology through Digital Public Goods (DPGs). But DPG recognition guarantees the integrity of the supply side — open licensing, privacy, and related standards — not that a solution will actually work in the field: in the first 72 hours of a disaster response, in the daily operations of a refugee camp, or in a municipality rebuilding after conflict.
This closing keynote of FOSS4G 2026 brings together speakers from various United Nations entities to share how technology is really being used in their operational contexts — and what is still missing. Together, the talks trace the value chain through which technology becomes real value on the ground: the frameworks that make openness a strategy, the capacity building that turns tools into skills, the technology transfer that grows local industries, the practice of delivering data in moments of crisis, and finally the people — those who have been beneficiaries of technology becoming its makers and its workforce.
Each speaker closes with one answer to a single shared question: what technology does your field still need? A moderated discussion then delivers those answers directly to the open-source community in the room. Held in Hiroshima, this session closes the conference by landing the story of technology on the story of human dignity.
